summary: Billing misalignment after SLO-triggered model fallback caused subset of requests billed at hosted tariff
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports an unexplained $37.15 line on their latest provisional invoice after an SLO-triggered fallback event. They say a small percentage of traffic that hit their dedicated pool was routed to hosted-backed variants and billed at hosted tariffs instead of being covered by reserved capacity credits. Impact: unexpected charge and incorrect credit attribution for March 9 maintenance window.

Environment: prod-us-east, Novametrics dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-evg-09), reserved hours active during period.

Timeline: 2026-03-09 22:31 UTC — Dedicated pool experienced transient latency spike; SLO policy auto-routed traffic to fallback model variants. 2026-03-09 22:31–22:45 UTC — ~2.4% of requests routed through hosted fallback. 2026-03-10 — Novametrics noticed extra line on provisional invoice and opened this ticket.

Steps to reproduce (customer-facing):
1) Trigger SLO threshold via synthetic load against dedicated pool.
2) Observe policy routing to hosted variant (fallback).
3) Check provisional invoice / hourly postbacks for the minute buckets matching failover window.

Observed behavior: A subset of requests routed to hosted fallback appear in billing as hosted-tariff line items and were not offset by the customer's reserved capacity credits. Billing records show the postbacks for those minute buckets as coming from the hosted-postback queue rather than the dedicated-postback namespace.

Expected behavior: Fallback routing should still record origin tags such that requests attributed to the customer's pool within the reserved time window are billed at reserved/dedicated rates or credited appropriately. Postback reconciliation should preserve org/pool tags even when routing changes target model variants.

Logs / supporting data: Customer provided example request IDs: req-20260309-223412-9f1a, req-20260309-223458-4b6c. Billing trace shows hosted_tariff rate_id: HSTD-2026-03 and missing reserved_tag: reserved_pool=ded-evg-09 for the affected postbacks. Router logs: fallback decision logged for routing-rule-id: slo-evg-fallback-3.

Attachments: provisional_invoice_2026-03-10.pdf (customer attached), sample_postback_jsons.txt (customer-supplied).

Requested outcome: Reclassify the affected postbacks to use reserved rate / apply retrospective credits for the $37.15 charge and root-cause to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC - Customer (Marcus Li): We saw a small hosted charge on our provisional invoice for the March 9 evening window. We were on reserved hours and expected zero hosted tariff usage — can you confirm why ~2% of traffic was billed? Attached invoice and two request IDs.

2026-03-10 10:02 UTC - Support (Arielle Park): Thanks Marcus, filing ticket SUP-309871 and routing to billing + infra. Can you confirm the dedicated pool id and any recent routing policy changes? We have the two request IDs; we'll pull postback traces.

2026-03-10 13:35 UTC - Engineering (Diego Morales): Initial triage: router logs confirm SLO-triggered fallback at 2026-03-09 22:31. Postback entries for affected minute buckets are present but many are missing reserved_pool tag; looks like the postback writer for hosted fallback did not propagate the reserved attribution header. Raised infra PR to add defensive copy of origin tags (see PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1223).

2026-03-11 08:21 UTC - Billing (Priya Shah): Observed hosted-rate line items totaling $37.15 for Novametrics provisional invoice. If we can reclassify those postbacks to the reserved tag, we can issue a provisional credit; final invoice adjustments require reconciliation window approval. Holding for eng confirmation and patch rollout schedule.

2026-03-12 16:03 UTC - Support (Arielle Park): Engineering has a hotfix staged in prod; estimated rollout 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. We will backfill attribution for affected postbacks for the 2026-03-09 22:31–22:45 minute buckets once the patch is deployed and then instruct Billing to issue the provisional credit. Please confirm if a waiver or immediate credit is preferred pending reconciliation.
2026-03-12 16:15 UTC - Customer (Marcus Li): Thanks — please apply provisional credit while you reconcile. We'd like follow-up on why origin tags were dropped during fallback.
investigation_notes:
Confirmed: router rule slo-evg-fallback-3 fired and routed subset to hosted-backed variant.
Hypothesis: hosted postback writer bypassed reserved-origin header when serializing postbacks, causing postbacks to be consumed by the hosted postback queue and flagged with hosted_tariff rate_id.
Evidence: sample postback JSON (customer-supplied) missing reserved_pool field; corresponding router trace contains reserved_pool but writer config override nullified header.
Impact quantification: 2.4% of traffic during 14-minute window (~1,480 calls) billed at hosted rates leading to $37.15 provisional line.
Mitigation: roll out patch to postback writer to always copy origin attribution header. Also add unit test around fallback path to assert reserved tags preserved.
Risk: low — change confined to postback writer path in hosted fallback; patch includes feature flag for quick rollback.
resolution_notes:
Action plan: deploy infra PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1223 to prod on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC (feature-flagged). After successful rollout, run backfill job to reclassify affected postbacks for customer Novametrics for minute buckets 2026-03-09 22:31–22:45.
Billing: after reclassification, Billing (Priya Shah) to apply provisional credit of $37.15 and note for reconciliation window so final invoice will not include the hosted-tariff charge.
Follow-up: add monitoring alert for any postback missing reserved_pool attribution when customer has active reserved hours. Documented runbook update at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/1156/SLO+Fallback+Routing+Runbook.
Status: In Progress — patch staged, backfill and credit pending successful deployment and verification.
